subject: Quality/latency spike impacting checkout - possible SLA claim
messages:
From: Aaron Patel <aaron@shopgrid.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@shopgrid.com
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quality/latency spike impacting checkout - possible SLA claim

Hi Diego,

We noticed a pronounced spike in 5xxs and tail latency that affected our checkout flow last night (UTC window below). Our analytics show ~6% checkout failures and a 3x increase in P99 latency between 2029-06-16 23:57 UTC and 2029-06-17 00:23 UTC. This materially impacted revenue during a promo period.

Can Redwood confirm the exact window on your side and advise whether this qualifies as an SLA event for pro-rata credit? We need a confirmation timeline and the next steps for evidence submission — procurement is prepared to pause invoicing for the affected interval pending confirmation.

I've attached a screenshot of our merchant dashboard and included a short list of example request ids: req_9f3a, req_9f4b, req_9f9d. We can share traces if you need them.

Thanks,
Aaron Patel
Head of Payments, ShopGrid
aaron@shopgrid.com
(attachment: checkout_errors.png)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quality/latency spike impacting checkout - possible SLA claim

Hi Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the example request ids. I'm sorry ShopGrid hit this during a promo.

I've opened an internal support record (SUP-3482) and looped the SLA/product teams. To move this forward we need:
- Full request traces (curl/http headers) for a handful of failing requests (the req ids you listed are perfect).
- Any client-side timeout configuration you had in place.
- Whether this workload was pinned to Redwood Dedicated or using the hosted pool for that period.

If you can drop the traces into the support thread or share a Drive link, we'll pull the server-side traces and an availability window. We'll also flag billing so procurement can hold settlement until eligibility is determined.

I'll follow up with a confirmation of the window once we correlate traces.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — adding a few notes on evidence and timeline. Aaron, copying the key items we need to verify eligibility:

1) Customer evidence (you):
   - Full request/response traces for failing requests (including X-Redwood-ReqId if present)
   - A short list of representative timestamps (you already gave some req ids which is helpful)
   - Any proxy/load-balancer logs on your side if available

2) Redwood evidence (we will pull):
   - Token-level latency histograms and instance-level 5xx counts for the window
   - Inference shard allocations and any autoscaler events (evictions/preemptions)
   - Server traces correlated to the provided req ids

3) Eligibility notes:
   - Hosted (shared pool) and Dedicated customers have different remedies; please confirm which you were on.
   - If this is a transient degraded window (sub-hour) we typically evaluate pro-rata credit per the SLA; persistent regressions may trigger a larger remediation discussion.

Timeline: we'll aim to produce an initial verification (window + preliminary eligibility) within 48 business hours after we have the traces. If eligible, finance will be looped to calculate the pro-rata credit and Marissa will scope the postmortem (PMO).

Diego — please mark SUP-3482 as high priority. Aaron — if you can upload the traces to the support ticket or share them here, that'll speed things up.

—Karthik
Senior Incident Response, Redwood Inference

Hi Aaron — I'm Marissa from Product Operations, thanks for the details and apologies for the impact. A quick summary and next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

Summary so far:
- Reported impact window (ShopGrid): 2029-06-16 23:57 UTC -> 2029-06-17 00:23 UTC
- Support ticket: SUP-3482
- Evidence requested: customer traces + our server-side traces and histograms

Preliminary eligibility: based on initial telemetry this appears to be a transient availability/latency regression that could qualify for a pro-rata credit under the regional SLA. Final determination will depend on the correlated traces and whether the traffic was routed to a degraded hardware pool.

Attachments: I've attached an evidence specification that outlines the exact artifacts we need (evidence_spec.md). Please upload your traces to the SUP-3482 thread or share a secure Drive link. Once we have them, we will:
- Correlate req ids and produce an official downtime/degraded-window confirmation
- Calculate pro-rata credit (finance will produce the invoice adjustment)
- Share a PMO scope and timeline for the postmortem (we aim to publish an RCA within 10 business days of full evidence receipt)

If procurement needs an official hold notice for billing, we can provide a short written hold confirming the investigation is in progress. Let me know and I'll send it.

Apologies again — we'll prioritize SUP-3482 and get you a formal eligibility determination ASAP.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
